method: ICU76 ubidi_setPara paragraph level1 for Arabic/Urdu, level0 for Bengali; ubidi_writeReordered; controls stripped only from diagnostic visual output

whole_run_isolate_comparison.why_not_chosen: LRI changes the whole spoken-count display to LTR numbering, while both existing options use localized conjunctions and RTL reading order. This is not a pure LTR numeric/musical notation run. No demonstrated defect in that shared convention justifies uniquely reorienting this distractor. For any future decision to force a notation-style LTR count, review all three options together; do not blanket-format prose.

cases.decision: Propose no new directional marks. Both adjacent same-quiz count options already begin with the same local count label and use the same conjunction, without marks. Under RTL paragraph level1 their digits appear physically right-to-left, which follows local-language reading order; reverse left-to-right diagnostic digit order alone is not a defect. Adding LRI to this option alone would introduce a different presentation convention.
cases.required_device_check: Verify in the actual RTL quiz that reading from the right gives counts1,2,3,and4 and that the conjunction is grouped after3, comparing both sibling options. Check accessibility spoken order and forced/automatic paragraph direction. If the UI presents counts as LTR notation, independently review a coordinated whole-quiz change; this proposal does not certify it.
cases.certification: ICU76 Unicode-order diagnostic only, not native-human approval or actual iOS layout/font/VoiceOver evidence.

cases.decision: Bengali uses LTR writing. Old and new digit visual order remains1,2,3,4 at paragraph level0; replacing ও with আর matches both adjacent spoken-count choices. No bidi controls needed.
cases.required_device_check: Confirm Bengali glyph shaping, comma spacing and offbeat আর pronunciation/placement in the quiz; independent semantic/device review still pending.
cases.certification: ICU76 Unicode-order diagnostic only, not native-human approval or actual iOS layout/font/VoiceOver evidence.
